best_for: Windows and Mac users who want an encrypted alternative to Dropbox or OneDrive, and who already use, or would pay for, other Proton apps.

points.title: 5 GB free, 200 GB for a few dollars
points.text: Proton Free includes 5 GB and needs no credit card. Drive Plus gives 200 GB for USD 2.49 per month on a 12-month plan (USD 29.88 the first year, then USD 47.88 a year) and keeps old file versions for 10 years. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Bigger plans bundle the other apps
points.text: Proton Unlimited gives 500 GB plus Mail, Calendar, VPN and Pass for USD 6.49 per month (USD 77.88 the first year, then USD 119.88). Duo gives 2 TB for two people at USD 14.99 per month billed yearly, and Family lists 3 TB for up to six people at USD 29.99 per month. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Works from File Explorer
points.text: On Windows the app adds a Proton Drive folder to File Explorer, syncs chosen folders in the background, and has an Optimize storage setting to free local space. It can also import photos from a local folder or from Google Photos.

points.title: A Proton account is required
points.text: You sign in with a Proton account before anything syncs. You cannot create folders at the root of the Proton Drive folder; your files go under My files, and other synced computers appear under Other computers, up to 10.

points.title: No Linux desktop app
points.text: Proton's download page offers desktop apps for Windows and macOS only. Linux users get a command-line tool (also offered for Windows and macOS) or the web app, and nothing is listed for Linux here.

points.title: Installs per user, Arm64 included
points.text: The Windows installer is per-user, in x64 and Arm64 builds for Windows 10 and 11. The Mac app is one universal build that needs macOS 13 or later. The Windows listing keeps 56 versions; macOS lists only the current release.
